items.q: What story does Squibb say you have to tell first?
items.a: The **real why**. His: father died at 15, kicked out, homeless, social services said no — he **needed** a business. Don't copy someone else's identity. If you are not there yet, **share the struggle and learn in public** instead of guru-cosplay.

items.q: What does 'tailor-made for the platform' actually mean?
items.a: **Edit inside the app** (captions + hook). Snapchat now **labels recorded-in-app vs uploaded**. Instagram Stories should be **shot in the moment**, not a standard video dumped into Stories. Make the app believe the file was born there.

items.q: Why sit in the comments instead of posting and leaving?
items.a: Every major app **rewards creator–audience threads**. Reply yourself; use **ManyChat** (not a sponsor) if volume requires it. Answer **and/or ask back**. Ten minutes then leaving is leaving distribution on the table.

items.q: What two data camps does he split social into?
items.a: **Video graph:** hook, finish, rewatch — if it dies, **recut and republish**. **Owned list:** a **thousand emails** you can actually message beat **a million views** with no relationship, because a platform can suppress you tomorrow.

items.q: What habit does he say people reject, and how long did he run it?
items.a: **Daily posting. No passive income.** Six years. First TikTok: him and his son at the zoo learning filters. Batch-record if you cannot shoot daily. The streak turns attention into trust — then you still need a way to take the money.

items.q: How do you staff social before you can pay salaries?
items.a: Treat it as a **team sport**: camera, editor, story structure, poster (seats can collapse into one person). **Share the upside** — e.g. 50% of a chess channel's revenue. He'd rather **10% of something that matters** than **100% of a grind he hates**.
